question: A 12-month-old boy who presents a right testicle in the inguinal canal during health examinations performed since birth, and it is not possible to descend to the scrotum. Point out the CORRECT answer:

options.opa: The most probable diagnosis is the retractable testicle.
options.opb: It is necessary to wait until two years of age to occur spontaneous descent of it.
options.opc: Human chorionic gonadotropin is the treatment of first choice.
options.opd: The indication of orchidopexy should not be deferred.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Right testicle in inguinal canal" -> "Not possible to descend to scrotum" -> "Consistent with undescended testicle" -> "Orchidopexy recommended" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Right testicle in inguinal canal" -> "Not possible to descend to scrotum" -> "Unlikely to be retractable testicle" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Right testicle in inguinal canal" -> "Not descended by 12 months" -> "Spontaneous descent unlikely after 6 months" -> "Waiting until two years not recommended" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Right testicle in inguinal canal" -> "Not possible to descend to scrotum" -> "Human chorionic gonadotropin not first choice" -> "Surgical intervention preferred" -> 80%
analysis: The scenario described is consistent with cryptorchidism, where the testicle has not descended into the scrotum. In such cases, orchidopexy is recommended to be performed between 6 and 18 months of age to reduce the risk of infertility and testicular cancer. Waiting until two years of age is not advised, and human chorionic gonadotropin is not the first-line treatment. A retractable testicle can be manually moved to the scrotum, which is not the case here. Therefore, the correct answer is that the indication of orchidopexy should not be deferred.
